chunks: Zurara narrated from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he said:

The prayer is not repeated except for five [pillars]: purification, time, direction of the qibla, bowing, and prostration. Then he said: 'Recitation is a sunnah and the tashahhud is a sunnah, so the sunnah does not break the obligatory duty.'
As for what indicates that if one forgets one of them and remembers it before bowing, it is obligatory to send himself [straight into it] and prostrate.
ai.seo_question: What are the five pillars of prayer that require repetition if missed, and how does one handle forgetting a pillar before bowing?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi uses this narration from Zurara to establish the fundamental distinction between fard (obligatory) and sunnah (recommended) components in Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing that the validity of the prayer hinges on the five core pillars. The text further clarifies the procedural ruling for nسيyan (forgetfulness), specifying that if a pillar is missed and remembered before entering ruku, the worshipper must simply proceed without invalidating the prayer, thereby preserving the integrity of the fard acts.
